_meta.purpose: Phase-D4+D5 golden set (BETA campaign) — same architecture as tests/eval/piet_d1 and piet_d2d3 (isolated per-case --do invocations, oracle-verbatim expected values, display-precision tolerances, standalone leg not wired into run_eval.py). UNLIKE the earlier legs, the D4/D5 wirings were ALREADY LANDED (op/piet @ff9d06a) when this leg was authored — this leg is the independent Eval-owned regression net documenting CURRENT STATUS (the golden-first RED proof for D4/D5 lives in the wirings' own oracle-pinned selftest legs on op/piet, not here). See CURRENT-STATUS.txt.
_meta.oracle_log: internal capture d45-oracle-stata.log (real StataBE 19.5, import delimited fatalities.csv, 336 obs; preamble: gen high=(beertax>.5) + encode state, gen(snum) + gen t=_n + tsset t). The 2026-08-01 professor-pangram additions use the user-run StataNow log at pangram_stata_results.log (internal capture); its prepared dataset ran xtset snum year before gen t=_n, so the physical panel/time sort is part of those two cases' oracle semantics.
_meta.dataset_loader: sysuse fatalities, clear (bundled sample, byte-identical to the oracle's import — established in piet_d1). Every case's do_body is fully self-contained (preamble included).

tolerance_policy.rationale: Same display-precision derivation as piet_d1/piet_d2d3. Worst display-precision pins in this leg: hausman chi2=2.62 (3 sig figs, ~1.9e-3 relative) and sdtest p_upper=.0258 (~1.9e-3) — both inside scalar_rtol=3e-3. Oracle p-values displayed as '0.0000' are pinned as 0.0 with the 1e-4 atol floor ONLY as SECONDARY checks (the engine emits the true tiny p, e.g. 4e-83, which passes |got-0|<=1e-4... it does not: 4e-83 <= 1e-4 is true — the atol floor is exactly what makes a '0.0000'-displayed p gradeable).
tolerance_policy.integer_and_string_fields: EXACT (lags, df, dof, G, group_sizes, case labels)

_meta.scalar_path_syntax: Scalar keys in required_scalars/exact_scalars/scalars are jget-style JSON paths into the estimation block: dots descend into dicts ('classic.F'), [name] matches an array element by its 'name' field ('firststage[beertax].F', 'coefs[beertax].diff'), [N] is a list index. A resolved SINGLE-ELEMENT LIST is unwrapped before numeric compare (estat durbinalt emits chi2/F/df/p as per-lag one-element arrays — live-verified @ff9d06a).
_meta.schema_provenance: ALL graded field names live-verified against op/piet @ff9d06a (2026-07-15) probe runs: newey (lag/df_r), prais (rho/dw/dw_0/method), dfuller & pperron (Zt/Zrho/cv_1/cv_5/cv_10/lags/newey_west_lags/case/p), wntestq (Q/df/lags/p), sdtest (F/df1/df2/p/p_lower/p_upper/sd_1/sd_2/combined.*), estat durbinalt (chi2/F/df/df_r/p arrays), estat firststage (firststage[{name,F}]), margins-dydx (coeftable), hausman (chi2/p/dof/coefs[{name,b_fe,b_re,diff}]), chow (classic.{F,df1,df2}/G/group_sizes), mkspline (summarize stats shape), tsfill (count -> display blocks).
_meta.check_severity_model: Same as piet_d2d3: coefs + n_obs (where declared) + required_scalars + exact_scalars are FATAL; 'scalars' are SECONDARY (absent = note, present-but-wrong = fatal); unpinned_oracle_reference blocks are NOT GRADED (oracle values the landed schema demonstrably does not emit, or values deliberately not pinned).

unpinned_oracle_reference.__why: the landed newey block carries no F field (live-verified)

d4a_newey_lag2.notes: Newey-West HAC SEs at lag(2). The b's equal plain OLS by construction; the HAC se's (353.9058 vs OLS's 211.8775 for beertax) are the actual signal the lag window is applied.

unpinned_oracle_reference.__why: the landed prais block carries no F/r2/rmse fields (live-verified); dw/dw_0 ARE carried and pinned

d4b_prais_twostep.notes: Prais-Winsten (twostep): n_obs stays 336 (first obs retained via the PW transform). dw_0 = Stata's 'Durbin-Watson statistic (original)', dw = '(transformed)'.

d4a2_newey_lag2_after_xtset_sort.stata: xtset snum year; gen t=_n; tsset t; newey income beertax spirits, lag(2)
d4a2_newey_lag2_after_xtset_sort.notes: Pins Stata's physical-sort side effect of xtset. The standalone d4a case remains valid for raw CSV row order; this case deliberately xtsets before generating t=_n, so a metadata-only xtset yields the old wrong se=353.9057519462703 and fails.

d4b2_prais_twostep_after_xtset_sort.stata: xtset snum year; gen t=_n; tsset t; prais income beertax, twostep
d4b2_prais_twostep_after_xtset_sort.notes: Companion physical-sort pin to d4a2. A metadata-only xtset leaves raw CSV order and produces the old wrong rho=.8034460644, b=-1997.2434770, se=281.7460888; the corrected Stata-compatible sort must reach this oracle instead.

d4b_prais_corc.notes: Cochrane-Orcutt (iterated): n_obs=335 EXACT — CO drops the first observation, PW keeps it; the 336-vs-335 pair across the two prais cases is the sharpest twostep-vs-corc semantic check. Different converged rho (.8038 vs .8034) confirms genuine iteration.

d4c_dfuller_bare.notes: Bare Dickey-Fuller (no lags, no trend — Stata's 'Random walk without drift' case). The MacKinnon approximate p displays as 0.0000 in the oracle; pinned 0.0 as SECONDARY under the 1e-4 atol floor (the engine emits the true tiny p).

d4c_dfuller_lags2_trend.notes: Augmented DF with 2 lags + trend: DIFFERENT critical-value row than the bare case (-3.987/-3.427/-3.130 vs -3.453/-2.877/-2.570) — proves the cv table actually switches on the deterministic-term case, not just echoes one hardcoded row. n_obs drops to 333 (2 lags + 1 difference).

unpinned_oracle_reference.__why: the landed pperron block emits ONE cv set (the Zt row); Stata's separate Z(rho) critical-value row is not carried (live-verified) — recorded for a future schema extension

d4d_pperron.notes: Phillips-Perron: both Z(rho) and Z(t) statistics pinned; default Newey-West lag choice (5 = trunc(4*(n/100)^(2/9))) pinned EXACT as the bandwidth-selection proof.

d4e_wntestq_bare.notes: Portmanteau Q, default lag choice (min(n/2-2, 40) = 40 here) — df=40 EXACT is the default-lag-rule proof.

d4e_wntestq_lags10.notes: Explicit lags(10) — different Q and df than the bare case proves the option forwards.

d4f_tsfill_gapfill.oracle_section: D4f (coordinator-adapted fixture: drop t in [100,106], NOT the oracle's mod(t,7) — mod() is unimplemented until Phase G)
d4f_tsfill_gapfill.stata: drop if t>=100 & t<=106  ->  count (329)  ->  tsfill  ->  count (336)
d4f_tsfill_gapfill.notes: Mechanical gap-fill semantics: dropping the 7 interior periods t=100..106 leaves 329 obs; tsfill must restore the panel to exactly 336 rows (new rows with missing data). Graded off the two `count` display blocks in order. The oracle's own construction used mod(t,7) (dropping 48 obs, restoring interior gaps to 335) — deliberately NOT mirrored per the coordinator's directive because mod() is unimplemented in PIET until Phase G; the [100,106] contiguous-gap variant tests the same tsfill semantics with arithmetic PIET supports today (live-verified: 329 -> 336).

d5a_sdtest_by.notes: Variance-ratio test by group. p = Stata's two-sided 2*Pr(F>f)=0.0516, p_lower = Pr(F<f)=0.9742, p_upper = Pr(F>f)=0.0258 (field mapping live-verified). df 229/105 EXACT.

d5b_durbinalt_chi2.stata: regress income beertax spirits  ->  estat durbinalt
d5b_durbinalt_chi2.notes: Durbin's alternative, default (chi2 form, 1 lag). The block's chi2/df/p are per-lag ONE-ELEMENT ARRAYS (live-verified) — the driver's path resolver unwraps single-element lists before compare.

d5b_durbinalt_small_lags2.stata: regress income beertax spirits  ->  estat durbinalt, small lags(2)
d5b_durbinalt_small_lags2.notes: small -> F form instead of chi2 (F(2,331)=189.005); lags(2) -> df=2. The F-vs-chi2 switch plus the df pair is the whole point of this second case.

d5c_estat_firststage.stata: ivregress 2sls income emppop (beertax = spirits unemp)  ->  estat firststage

unpinned_oracle_reference.__why: the landed block carries ONLY the first-stage F per endogenous regressor, with an honest note field disclosing that R-sq/partial-R-sq/min-eigenvalue/critical-value table are not computed (not fabricated) — live-verified. The Stock-Yogo cv table is likewise not carried.

d5c_estat_firststage.notes: First-stage F (2,332)=2.56678 pinned via the firststage[beertax].F path. No n_obs field on this block (postestimation summary) — n_obs check omitted.

d5d_margins_dydx_logit.stata: logit high income unemp  ->  margins, dydx(income)
d5d_margins_dydx_logit.notes: Average marginal effect of income after logit: dydx -.0001192, delta-method se .0000112 — REAL logit AMEs (the engine's margins dydx path handles non-OLS models; contrast the at() case below, where the predictive-margins path does not).

d5d_margins_at_logit.stata: logit high income unemp  ->  margins, at(income=13000)
d5d_margins_at_logit.notes: Pr(high) at income=13000 after logit — Stata's predictive margin (the oracle values recorded as `unpinned_oracle_reference` when this case was a REJECT). d5e_hausman_fe_re.stata: xtreg fe -> estimates store feM -> xtreg re -> store reM -> hausman feM reM

unpinned_oracle_reference.__why: sqrt(diag(V_b-V_B)) per-coef SEs are not carried in the landed hausman block (live-verified: coefs rows have b_fe/b_re/diff only)

d5e_hausman_fe_re.notes: The full estimates-store idiom: two xtreg fits, two named stores, hausman by store name. chi2(2)=2.62, p=.2697. The landed block's n_obs is 0 (postestimation-block quirk, live-verified) — n_obs check deliberately omitted rather than pinning a meaningless 0. Per-coef diffs pinned via coefs[name].diff paths.

d5f_chow_by_high.stata: PIET: chow income beertax, by(high)  — vs the oracle's manual pooled/split RSS formula

unpinned_oracle_reference.__why: derivable from the oracle's sub-regressions (rss_p=1.4318e+09; rss_0+rss_1=869786133+354907320) and matched by the block's classic.ssr_* fields to ~7 digits, but the oracle log only displays them at 5 sig figs — the F (computed by Stata at full precision, displayed to 8 digits via the di line) is the sharper pin. The block's 'robust' sub-object (HC1 chow variant) has NO Stata oracle and is not graded.

d5f_chow_by_high.notes: Real Stata has NO chow command — the oracle is a manual F construction (pooled vs split-sample RSS: F=((rss_p-rss_0-rss_1)/k)/((rss_0+rss_1)/(n-2k))=28.074171, df 2/332, computed in StataBE and displayed via di at 8 digits). PIET's `chow ..., by()` convenience wrapper must reproduce exactly that classic formula in its classic.* sub-object (live-verified it does, to 10 significant digits).

d5g_mkspline_knots_mech.oracle_section: D5g (explicit-knots form — NO oracle numbers by design)
d5g_mkspline_knots_mech.notes: MECHANICAL-PASS ONLY (coordinator directive): the explicit knots() form runs and materializes the k-1=3 cubic-spline basis variables, each with N=336 and no missings. The knot values (11000/13000/15000/17000) are Eval-chosen round numbers with NO Stata oracle — the oracle only ran nknots(4), whose default knot PLACEMENT (percentile-based) was not recorded, so no numeric pin is possible for the explicit form without a new StataBE run (note-don't-guess). Numeric spline-basis parity is deferred to the nknots case's future flip (below).

d5g_mkspline_nknots.oracle_section: D5g (nknots(4) — FLIPPED 2026-07-15: Phase-F engine fix computes correct percentile knot placement; oracle numbers now graded)
d5g_mkspline_nknots.stata: mkspline inc_sp = income, cubic nknots(4)  ->  regress high inc_sp1 inc_sp2 inc_sp3 (check regression)

unpinned_oracle_reference.__why: knot placement (5/35/65/95 pctiles) and the basis summarize stats have no gradable path in this driver: mkspline itself emits no 'estimation'-type block, and the driver's mechanical summarize_check (see d5g_mkspline_knots_mech) only compares N, not mean/sd — recorded here for provenance only. The actual numeric gate for correct knot placement is the check-regression's inc_sp1/inc_sp2/inc_sp3 coefficients above (required_scalars), which ARE knot-placement-sensitive. _cons is recorded but not gated: informational only, and it sidesteps the coeftable name-alias question for '_cons' under this driver's bracket-path jget, which — unlike the 'coefs' b+se convenience dict used by other cases — does NOT apply the _cons/(intercept) alias.

d5g_mkspline_nknots.notes: FLIPPED 2026-07-15 from reject to golden: Phase-F engine fix (branch op/cobra-beta-f @d2588a9) landed correct percentile knot placement for mkspline nknots() (previously errored 'need at least 3 knots' before computing anything — see the prior reject-pin this replaces). Oracle: internal note f-oracle-pins.md §mkspline (StataBE 19.5, captured 2026-07-15): nknots(4) knots = 5/35/65/95 pctiles of income = {10745.9, 12815.69, 14541.8, 18077.87}. No independent se's were recorded for the check regression, so the coefficient check is graded via required_scalars (b only, coeftable[name].b jget paths) rather than the stricter 'coefs' b+se dict used elsewhere in this file. Case id dropped its '_reject' suffix (was d5g_mkspline_nknots_reject) to match the leg's own convention that a plain (unsuffixed) id denotes a golden case, mirroring d5g_mkspline_knots_mech's '_mech' suffix for its mechanical kind.
